items.title: Verified-receipt evaluation package for administrative barriers to benefit access
items.description: A reusable method for designing, adapting and evaluating assistance or process changes that aim to raise verified benefit receipt. It defines the outcome stages, comparison requirements, harms and local adaptation checks that any qualified, authorised institution would need before testing an intervention.
items.scientificRationale: Linked abstract-level evidence suggests hands-on compliance assistance can raise verified receipt in some settings, while information-only outreach often moves applications more than receipt. The package therefore makes verified receipt the primary outcome and treats applications as an intermediate stage.
evidenceLimitations: Linked studies are predominantly from the United States and Western Europe.
Extraction is abstract-level; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.
Reviews E03 and E04 overlap with each other and with primary trials; study counts must not be added.
contextDependencies: Eligibility rules and whether access is claim-based or registration-based.
Existing advice services and their capacity.
Administrative data availability for verified receipt.
resourcePrerequisites: Trained advisers or agency process owners
Budget for delivery and independent evaluation
institutionalPrerequisites: Lawful access to verified receipt records
Agreement with the administering agency where process changes are tested
potentialBenefits: Higher verified receipt of lawful entitlements
Reduced time and cost for claimants

primaryOutcome.definition: Proportion of independently verified eligible participants confirmed as receiving the specified benefit within a prespecified follow-up window.

secondaryOutcomes.definition: Time and out-of-pocket cost of benefit navigation.
Equity gaps in the primary outcome across prespecified, lawful and adequately powered groups.
Implementation and participant costs reported separately from incremental effects.

harmMeasures: Failed applications caused by the intervention
measurementPlan.comparisonRequirement: A prespecified comparison with usual services available to everyone; no legally owed benefit may be withheld from any group.
measurementPlan.missingData: Report attrition and missing receipt verification by arm; present worst/best-case bounds alongside any primary estimate.
measurementPlan.causalInference: Causal claims only from a prespecified, independently reviewed design. Observational comparisons are described as associations.
measurementPlan.sampleSize: Not calculated for any HPI context: requires a verified baseline receipt rate, a justified minimum meaningful difference and an approved design. The planning calculator on the solutions page is an aid, not a protocol.

items.title: Energy affordability research template
items.description: A scoped research definition for energy affordability that separates bills, adequate energy services, warmth, health and distributional effects.
items.scientificRationale: Linked evidence shows lower bills can coincide with underconsumption, and realised savings can fall below predictions; outcomes must capture adequate energy services, not spending alone.
evidenceLimitations: No context fact recorded for any HPI context.
resourcePrerequisites: Metered or billing data with consent

primaryOutcome.definition: Verified household energy expense divided by measured household resources in comparable periods.

secondaryOutcomes.definition: Validated measure of inability to afford adequate energy.

measurementPlan.comparisonRequirement: Prespecified comparison; weather and tariff changes accounted for.
measurementPlan.missingData: Report missing billing periods by group.
measurementPlan.causalInference: Causal claims only from approved designs.

evidence.note: Internal rapid evidence synthesis; not systematic and not independent.

missing: Context selection with recorded energy-burden facts

items.title: Livelihoods and job-quality research template
items.description: A scoped research definition requiring sustained net earnings, job quality and displacement measures rather than enrolment counts.
items.scientificRationale: Linked evidence includes fading gains, harmful jobs and small average training effects; durable outcomes and nonparticipant effects must be measured.
evidenceLimitations: Linked trials are mostly in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
No HPI context has linked livelihoods evidence.
institutionalPrerequisites: Implementing partner with verified earnings measurement

primaryOutcome.definition: Sustained net earnings adjusted to local prices.

measurementPlan.causalInference: Causal claims only from approved designs.
